titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 15, the hymns (part 1 of 4)
part: Spell 15 — the hymns, part 1 of 4: a hymn to Ra at his rising and the opening of a hymn to Osiris (Plates 18–19)
about: Spell 15 is a set of hymns sung to the sun and to Osiris; on Ani's papyrus it comes after Spell 10 on Plate 18 and runs on across Plate 19. This first part holds a hymn to Ra as he rises, spoken by Ani: the sun crosses the sky in his two barks, the stars praise him, his enemy is bound and cut down, and he is hailed as the one god who spoke the world out of silence. It ends with Ani's titles, and then a second hymn begins, to Osiris as lord of eternity, whom the sun's setting brings to the dead. Several signs in Budge's type are uncertain, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: adoring · Ra · at · rising · his · in · the-horizon · until · coming-about · setting · his · in · life
sentences.i: Adoring Ra at his rising in the horizon until his setting comes about, in life.
sentences.n: Spell 15 begins, and the papyrus writes its title in red, except the name of Ra and ꜣḫt 'horizon', which stand in black. dwꜣ 'adore, praise' is the star (dwꜣ) with the vulture ꜣ as complement, a standing man raising his arm in worship (approximated in the type) and the papyrus roll; as in the hymn on Plate 1 it is the infinitive, naming the act: 'adoring Ra'. rꜥ 'Ra' is written here with the seated god wearing the sun-disk alone. m wbn·f 'at his rising': after the preposition m, wbn 'rise' (quail chick w, foot b, water n, the sun as classifier) is the infinitive, and the suffix ·f 'his', the horned viper, is its subject. ꜣḫt 'horizon' is the sun between two hills, with t and a house-like sign as classifiers. r ḫpr ḥtp·f: r 'until' with the infinitive ḫpr 'come about' (scarab ḫpr, r as complement), whose subject is ḥtp·f 'his setting' (offering table ḥtp with t and p as complements, and ·f); ḥtp is 'be at peace, rest', and of the sun 'set'. m ꜥnḫ 'in life' (ankh with n and ḫ as complements): the sun goes down alive, to rise again. Spell 15 is a set of hymns to the sun and to Osiris; this is the first of them.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani:
sentences.n: ḏd in N 'said by N', in red, brings in the speaker. ḏd 'say' is the cobra ḏ and the hand d, printed as one ligature; in 'by', which names the one who speaks, is the reed i over the water n. Wsir 'the Osiris' is the low seat ws (coded Q2, an approximation of the type) over the eye ir, without the seated god, in black: the dead man bears the name of the god who died and lived again. sš 'scribe' is the palette with water-pot and pen; Budge reads it ān, but the palette is the regular sign of sš. ꜣny 'Ani' is vulture ꜣ, water n and two reeds y, with the seated man; the three small strokes under ꜣ-n belong to the usual writing of his name and are not read.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · Ra · in · rising · his · Atum · Horakhty
sentences.i: Hail to you, Ra, in his rising, Atum-Horakhty!
sentences.n: Ani's speech begins, in black. Budge prints ind-ḥr·k as one group; it is split here into the interjection and ḥr·k. ind 'hail, greetings' is the reed i and a post with a knobbed top and a side arm (the sign nḏ, Aa27, approximated in the type), with the papyrus roll; ḥr·k is the face ḥr with its stroke and the basket ·k 'you, your': literally 'greetings to your face'. rꜥ 'Ra' is the seated god with the sun-disk. m wbn·f 'in his rising' as in the title, here with the sun shedding rays (N8, approximate) as classifier: the god is greeted and then spoken of in the third person, as often in hymns. itm 'Atum' is the loaf t and the sledge tm (U15) with the seated god; the reed i of the name is not written (Budge: Tem). The falcon ḥr with two rounded oblongs each crossed by a stroke (coded N18 twice, an approximation; Budge reads χuti) is taken, with Budge, as ḥr-ꜣḫty 'Horakhty', 'Horus of the horizon', the doubled sign standing for the horizon; Budge prints Ḥeru and χuti apart, and they are joined here as one name. Atum is the sun as the old creator, Horakhty the sun standing above the horizon: one god under his names.

sentences.l: adoring · you · beauty · your · in · my-two-eyes · comes-into-being · radiance · upon · (my)-breast
sentences.i: Praise to you! Your beauty is in my eyes, and radiance comes to be upon (my) breast.
sentences.n: Budge prints dwꜣ-tw as one group; it is split here into the verb and tw 'you', the dependent pronoun (loaf t, quail chick w) that stands as the object. dwꜣ is the star with ꜣ as complement, a kneeling man with an arm raised (approximated) and the papyrus roll; no subject follows, so it is taken as the infinitive used as an exclamation, 'adoring you', 'praise to you'. Budge takes it as a passive, 'adored art thou'. nfrw·k 'your beauty' is the heart-and-windpipe nfr written three times, the plural used for an abstract noun, and ·k. m irty·i 'in my two eyes': the eye written twice is irty, the dual of irt 'eye', and the seated man is ·i 'my'; no sickle is printed, so the word is 'eyes', not mꜣꜣ 'see' (Budge reads maa-à). nfrw·k m irty·i is a sentence with no verb, 'your beauty (is) in my eyes'. ḫpr ꜣḫw is a sḏm·f with a noun subject, 'radiance comes into being': ꜣḫw 'radiance, sunlight' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ as complement, w, the sun shedding rays (approximate) and a stroke. ḥr šnbt 'upon the breast': ḥr is the face with its stroke, here the preposition 'upon'; šnbt 'breast' is the cord-loop šn (V7, approximate) with n, foot b, t and a fleshy curl (F51, approximate). No 'my' is written; Budge supplies it. The worshipper stands in the morning light and feels it on his body.

sentences.l: proceed · you · in · peace · your · in · the-Sektet-bark
sentences.i: You go on your way in your peace in the Sektet-bark;
sentences.n: wḏꜣ·k 'you proceed' is the quail chick w, a tall tapering sign taken as the fire-drill ḏꜣ (U28, approximate) and the walking legs, then ·k: the sḏm·f of wḏꜣ 'go on, set out'. m ḥtp·k 'in your peace': ḥtp (offering table, t, p) as a noun, with ·k; since ḥtp is also the sun's 'setting', 'at your setting' is possible, and Budge too was unsure of the ·k ('peace thy'). m sktt 'in the Sektet-bark' (Budge: sektet): the bolt s, the basket k, two loaves t and a boat with a cabin (approximated). The Sektet is the bark in which the sun travels; in these hymns it is paired with the Adjet-bark of the next line.

sentences.l: heart · your · is-glad · in · the-fair-wind · in · the-Adjet-bark · heart · its · is-sweet
sentences.i: your heart is glad with the fair wind in the Adjet-bark, and its heart is sweet.
sentences.n: ib·k ꜣw 'your heart is glad': ib is the heart with its stroke and ·k; ꜣw 'long, extended' is a hatched block on an arch with hanging cords (the spine sign ꜣw, F40, approximate), with w as complement and the papyrus roll, the stative after a noun subject. 'Long of heart' is the Egyptian way of saying glad. m mꜣꜥw 'with the fair wind': the sickle mꜣ, a low flat sign that this type prints where ꜥ is read (coded U15), w, a sail as the classifier of wind (approximate), the curl w again and plural strokes; mꜣꜥw is the wind that blows right for the boat, from mꜣꜥ 'true, right' (Budge: maāu, 'winds'). m ꜥḏt 'in the Adjet-bark' (Budge: āṭet) is the netting-needle sign ꜥḏ (V26, approximate) with the hand d, two t's and a boat, as on Plate 1; Budge's line numeral 4 is printed inside the word. ib·s nḏm 'its heart is sweet': ib·s is the heart with the bolt ·s 'its', the bark (a feminine noun); nḏm 'be sweet, pleasant' is printed with the same braided sign as the wick ḥ (coded V28, approximate) where the pod nḏm is expected, then m as complement and the roll; Budge reads net'em. The sun's boats sail on a wind that never fails.

sentences.l: (you)-traverse · the-sky · in · peace
sentences.i: (You) cross the sky in peace;
sentences.n: nmi 'traverse, travel across' is water n as complement, a slanting rod taken as the knife nm (T34, approximate), the owl m as complement and the reed i, then two classifiers: a square meander-like sign (coded O38, an approximation; it has no clear value) and the walking legs. No subject is written: Budge supplies [k] in his transliteration only, and the same words in line 8 have ·k. The suffix may have been left out, as often; the reading shows only what is printed, and the translation supplies '(you)'. ḥrt 'the sky' is the face ḥr with r, t and the sign of the sky. m ḥtpw 'in peace' is the offering table with t and p, two reeds, w and a stroke; the two reeds are not part of the usual spelling and are not read, with Budge (ḥetepu).

sentences.l: are-felled · enemies · your
sentences.i: your enemies are felled;
sentences.n: sḫr 'fell, overthrow' is the causative s- of ḫr 'fall': bolt s, placenta ḫ, mouth r and a man falling forward (approximated), then the low flat sign U15, here a classifier and not read. With a noun subject and no agent it is taken as the passive sḏm·f, 'are felled'. ḫftyw·k 'your enemies': placenta ḫ, viper f, loaf t and the vulture ꜣ, a kneeling man with an arm raised (the enemy, approximated), a small circle and plural strokes, then ·k. The vulture stands where the y of ḫfty is expected and is not read (Budge: χefta). The sun's enemies are struck down as he travels.

sentences.l: jubilate · to-you · the-Unwearying-Stars
sentences.i: the Unwearying Stars jubilate for you,
sentences.n: Budge prints hnw-n·k as one group; it is split here into hnw and n·k 'to you, for you' (water n and ·k). hnw 'jubilation, praise' is the shelter h, water n, the pot nw with w as complement and a kneeling man raising both arms (approximated), with a stroke; it is taken as a sḏm·f, 'they jubilate', with the short n·k before the noun subject, as short words go in Egyptian; as a noun it would give 'jubilation to you'. Budge prints h without a dot. iḫmw-wrd 'the Unwearying Stars' is two words that Budge prints apart and that are joined here as one name: iḫm 'not know' (reed i, chick w, placenta ḫ, owl m, with the arms held apart, the classifier of negation, approximated, and plural strokes; the w stands before ḫ in the print) and wrd 'be weary' (a long-tailed bird taken as wr, r, hand d, a weary seated man, a star and a seated god, with a stroke): 'those who do not know weariness'. They are the stars that never stop moving, the planets and the stars that rise and set.

sentences.l: adore · you · the-Imperishable-Stars · setting · in · the-horizon · of · Manu
sentences.i: and the Imperishable Stars adore you as you set in the horizon of Manu.
sentences.n: dwꜣ tw iḫmw-sk is built like dwꜣ tw ḥryw on Plate 1: verb, the pronoun tw 'you' as object, and the noun subject. Budge prints dwꜣ-tw as one group; it is split here. dwꜣ is the star with the standing worshipper (approximated) and the roll. iḫmw-sk 'the Imperishable Stars', 'those who do not know perishing', joins two of Budge's words: iḫm is written with the owl m before the placenta ḫ this time, and sk 'perish' is the bolt s as complement, a braided sign that the type prints like the wick ḥ (coded V28, approximate) where the sign sk (V29) is expected, the basket k as complement, a star and a stroke. They are the stars round the pole that never set. ḥtp 'setting' has no subject written; Budge supplies [thou]. It is taken as the infinitive used of what goes on at the time, 'as (you) set'. ḥtp is the offering table with t and p; Budge's numeral 6 stands before it. m ꜣḫt nt mꜣnw 'in the horizon of Manu': nt is the genitive 'of' in its feminine form, agreeing with ꜣḫt; mꜣnw 'Manu' is the sickle mꜣ with the pot nw written three times and the hill-country sign, the mountain of the west where the sun goes down.

sentences.l: beautiful · you · in · the-Two-Shrines(?) · lord · living · you · stable · as · lord · my
sentences.i: You are beautiful in the Two Shrines(?), O lord, living and enduring, my lord.
sentences.n: nfr·ṯi 'you are beautiful' is the heart-and-windpipe nfr with the tethering rope ṯ, the stative with its ending ·ṯi 'you' written short (the reed of ·ṯi is left out); Budge prints nefer-θà. ꜥnḫ·ṯi 'you are living' is the ankh with the same ending. The stative describes the state its subject is in. The next word is two dotted disks stacked (N5 N5); Budge reads àterti with his own query and gives 'the two halves of the sky'. It is read here, with the same doubt, as itrty 'the Two Shrines', the shrines of the south and the north that stand for the whole land; no sound sign is written, and another word for 'the two (times, days)' may lie behind the two suns. nb 'lord' (the basket) is an address. ḏd 'stable, enduring' is the djed pillar written twice, the second as classifier: the stative of ḏd 'be stable', with its ending unwritten; Budge reads ṭeṭṭeṭ. m nb·i 'as my lord': m is written with Aa15, then nb with the seated god and ·i, the seated man. Living and stable is what a god or a king is wished to be for ever.

morph.gloss: to be stable, enduring (verb; the djed pillar; stative ḏd 'stable')

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · Ra · at · rising · your · Atum · at · setting · your · beautiful
sentences.i: Hail to you, Ra, at your rising, Atum, at your beautiful setting!
sentences.n: A second greeting, built in two matching halves. Budge prints ind-ḥr·k as one group; it is split as in line 1. ind is the reed and the post nḏ (Aa27, approximate; printed here as a plain upright with a cross-petalled top) without the papyrus roll. m wbn·k 'at your rising' (Aa15 for m) now has ·k 'your': the god is spoken to directly; the sun-disk stands between the chick and the foot. itm 'Atum' is the loaf t, the sledge tm and the seated god, as before; Budge's numeral 7 stands before it. m ḥtp·k nfr 'at your beautiful setting': the adjective nfr (heart and windpipe, with f and r) follows the noun and its suffix. Ra and Atum are the rising and the setting sun.

sentences.l: rise · you · shine · you · upon · the-back · of-mother · your · having-appeared · you · as · king · of-the-gods
sentences.i: You rise and you shine upon the back of your mother, having appeared in glory as king of the gods.
sentences.n: wbn·k and psd·k are two sḏm·f forms, 'you rise, you shine'; in wbn·k the type prints water n before the foot b. psd 'shine' is p, the bolt s and the hand d, with a diagonal rod crossed by ribs (the backbone sign, F37, approximate) and the sun-disk as classifiers; it is spelled with the hand d where older writing has the cobra ḏ, as on Plate 1. ḥr psd mwt·k 'upon the back of your mother': psd 'back' is the same letters with the backbone as classifier, the word that the shining verb is written like; mwt is the vulture mwt with ·k. The mother is the sky-goddess Nut, whose body arches over the earth; the sun travels along her back. ḫꜥ·ṯi 'you having appeared in glory' is the stative with ·ṯi: the sun rising over a hill (N28, approximate) with the low flat sign U15 where the arm ꜥ is read as complement, the papyrus roll, the rope ṯ and the reed i. m nswt nṯrw 'as king of the gods': nswt is the sedge with t and n written after it, an honorific spelling, and nṯrw the flag written three times. Budge's numeral 8 stands before nṯrw.

sentences.l: has-made · Nut · greeting · to · face · your
sentences.i: Nut has made the gesture of welcome to your face.
sentences.n: ir·n nwt nyny 'Nut has made greeting': ir is the eye alone (iri 'do, make') and the water n after it is the n of the sḏm·n·f, the form of completed action, which stands before the noun subject. Budge prints àri and en as two words; they are joined here. nwt 'Nut' is written with water n, the sign of a town (O49), t, a stroke, the sign of the sky and a rearing cobra as classifier (approximated): the town sign writes niwt 'town', a word that sounds like the goddess's name, so it stands here for its sound; the same spelling comes in the hymn to Osiris below. nyny 'greet, welcome' is n and two strokes y written twice, with a standing man holding his arms out (approximated). n ḥr·k 'to your face': the preposition n and ḥr·k. Each morning the sky-goddess receives the sun she has borne.

sentences.l: embraces · you · Maat · at · the-two-times
sentences.i: Maat embraces you at both times of the day.
sentences.n: ḥpt tw mꜣꜥt is verb, the pronoun object tw and the noun subject, as ḥpt tw mꜣꜥt on Plate 1; Budge prints ḥpt-tw as one group, split here. ḥpt 'embrace' is the wick ḥ, p, t and the two embracing arms (approximated). mꜣꜥt 'Maat' is the sickle mꜣ, the low flat sign U15 where ꜥ is read, t, and as classifiers the plinth mꜣꜥ, a flat bar with a small tie and a stroke; no seated goddess is printed, and mꜣꜥt may be read 'right order' as much as the goddess. r trwy 'at the two times': tr 'time, season' is t and r as complements, a reed, the plant-stem sign tr (approximate), w and two strokes for the dual ending -wy, and two sun-disks for morning and evening; the reed before tr is not read. Maat, the right order of the world, holds the sun at dawn and at dusk.

sentences.l: traverse · you · the-sky · heart · your · is-glad
sentences.i: You cross the sky, your heart glad;
sentences.n: nmi·k 'you traverse' is the same verb as in line 4, with the same uncertain meander-like classifier (O38, approximate), and here the basket ·k is printed: the sḏm·f. ḥrt 'the sky' as before. ib·k ꜣw 'your heart is glad', as in line 3: the heart with ·k and the spine sign ꜣw (approximate) with w and the papyrus roll, a stative after its subject.

sentences.l: the-Lake · of-Desdes · comes-into-being · in · peace
sentences.i: the Lake of Desdes comes to be at peace.
sentences.n: mr 'lake, canal' is the canal sign with a small wedge (approximate) and a stroke; it is followed directly by its genitive, the name dsds 'Desdes' (Budge: Ṭes-Ṭes): the knife ds written twice, with the canal as classifier; Budge's numeral 9 stands before the canal. ḫpr 'come into being, become' (scarab and r) is a sḏm·f with mr dsds as its subject. m ḥtpw 'in peace' (Aa15 for m; the offering table with t, p, w, the roll and a stroke). Desdes is a lake of the sky the sun crosses; that its waters are calm means the voyage goes well.

sentences.l: the-Rebel · fallen
sentences.i: The Rebel has fallen;
sentences.n: sbiw 'the Rebel' (Budge: Sebàu) is a tall upright forked at the top, taken as the sign sbi (Aa26, approximate and doubtful), with a small circle and plural strokes. ḫr 'fallen' is placenta ḫ, mouth r and a man falling forward (approximated): the stative of ḫr 'fall' after its subject, with no ending written, as on Plate 1 (sbiw ḫr). The Rebel is the serpent enemy of the sun.

sentences.l: his-two-arms · bound · has-cut-off · the-knife · backbone · his
sentences.i: his arms are bound, and the knife has cut through his backbone.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ꜣ-q-s-ꜣ-w and s-ḥ-q; read qꜣs 'bound' and ḥsq 'cut off'. The first verb has the vulture ꜣ before q and again after s, with the curl w and the low flat sign U15 as classifier; Plate 1 has the same phrase, ꜥwy·f qꜣs 'his arms are bound', and the letters of qꜣs are all here, out of order. The second has s and ḥ the wrong way round, with q, a knife and U15 as classifiers; ḥsq is the verb for cutting off with a knife. Budge reads aqesau 'cut off' and seḥeq 'severed'. ꜥwy·f 'his two arms' is the low flat sign U15 written twice with a stroke between, standing where the arm ꜥ is read (Budge āāui-f), and ·f. qꜣs is the stative after its subject. ḥsq·n is the sḏm·n·f: the water n after the verb, which Budge prints as a word of its own, is joined to it here. dmt 'knife' (Budge: ṭemt) is the hand d, Aa15 m, t and a knife, the subject. ṯst·f 'his backbone' is the tethering sign ṯs (S24) with the bolt s as complement, t, a fleshy curl (approximate), a stroke and ·f (Budge: θeset-f, 'his sinews'). The enemy of the sun is bound and butchered.

sentences.l: is · Ra · in · a-fair-wind · good
sentences.i: Ra is in a good fair wind;
sentences.n: wnn 'be, exist' is the hare wn with water n as complement and a second n: a sḏm·f, with rꜥ 'Ra' as its subject; wnn N m … is 'N is in …'. rꜥ is spelled here with the mouth r over the low flat sign U15 (where ꜥ is read), with the seated god. m mꜣꜥw nfr 'in a good fair wind': mꜣꜥw as in line 3, here with a loaf t where line 3 has the chick w; it is taken as the same word, and the t is not read. nfr 'good' follows its noun; Budge's numeral 10 stands before it.

sentences.l: the-Sektet-bark · has-hauled(?) · it · arrives · he · is-towed
sentences.i: the Sektet-bark has hauled on(?); he comes in under tow.
sentences.n: sktt, the Sektet-bark, now has a boat with mast and sail as classifier (approximated). It is named first and taken up again by the suffix in sk·n·s: sk is the bolt s as complement, the braided sign printed like the wick ḥ (coded V28, approximate) where the sign sk is expected, the basket k as complement and U15 as classifier, then water n and the bolt ·s 'it, she', the bark. As a sḏm·n·f, 'it has hauled'; the sense 'haul, tow' of sk is taken from Budge ('draweth on') and is not certain, and sk n·s, 'one hauls for it', is also possible. pḥ sw: pḥ 'reach, arrive' is the hindquarters of a lion (approximate) with the walking legs; sw is the sedge sw with w, the dependent pronoun 'he'. It is read 'he arrives', with sw as subject as in later Egyptian; 'it (the bark) reaches him' is also possible. stꜣ·tw 'he is towed' joins two of Budge's groups: stꜣ 'drag, tow' is the bolt s, t, a small cup taken for the sign tꜣ (W10, approximate), the vulture ꜣ as complement and w, with the coiled cord and the walking legs as classifiers; then t and w, the ending of the passive sḏm·tw·f. The w after ꜣ is not read. The sun's boat is hauled along by towing-ropes, as boats on the Nile were.

sentences.l: those-of-the-south · of-the-north · of-the-west · of-the-east · upon · adoring · you
sentences.i: Those of the south, the north, the west and the east are adoring you.
sentences.n: Four nisbas, adjectives made from nouns with -y and used as plural nouns, 'those of the south …': šmꜥyw is a tall stem with a hooked top crossing the low flat sign U15 (the sign šmꜥ, M26, approximate; Budge's qemāiu is his old value for it), two strokes y, a small wedge, w and a stroke; mḥtyw is the papyrus-roll-and-stem sign mḥ (V22, approximate), t, the vulture ꜣ and a stroke; imntyw is the emblem of the West with t, ꜣ, a stroke and the hill-country sign; iꜣbtyw is the emblem of the East with b, two t's and the hill-country sign. In the second and third the vulture ꜣ stands for the ending (Budge: meḥtaiu, àmentaiu) and is not read; in the fourth the second t stands where the ending is expected. Budge supplies '[the gods of]'. ḥr dwꜣ·k 'are adoring you': ḥr 'upon' with an infinitive says what is going on, and ·k after the infinitive is its object. Budge's numeral 11 is printed between the roll and ·k. All the beings of the four quarters worship the sun.

sentences.l: Primeval-One · of-forms · who-sends-forth · the-voice · the-earth · flooded · with · silence
sentences.i: O Primeval One of the forms of being, who sent forth the voice while the earth lay flooded with silence;
sentences.n: pꜣwty 'the Primeval One' is a bird with wings raised, alighting (the sign pꜣ, G41, approximate), then two small dotted disks, coded as the round loaf pꜣwt (X6) by the house ruling for this word (the shape is the same as the sun-disk N5), and the seated god: the nisba of pꜣwt 'primeval time', 'he who belongs to the first time', with its ending unwritten. Budge reads pautti and gives 'the double Paut'; the second disk is taken as a classifier written twice, not as a dual. ḫprw 'forms, ways of coming into being' (scarab, r, w, a standing wrapped figure, the roll and a stroke) follows directly as its genitive. wd 'who sends forth' is the chick w and the hand d with a small cross and U15 as classifiers: the participle of wdi 'put, cast, send out'. ḫrw 'the voice' is the oar ḫrw with w and the man with hand to mouth. tꜣ bꜥḥ m sgr: tꜣ 'the earth' (land with grains) and bꜥḥ 'flooded', a heron on a perch (G32, approximate), the word-sign of bꜥḥ 'flood', as a stative: 'the earth being flooded'. sgr 'silence' is the bolt s, a stand taken as the jar-stand g (W11, approximate), r and the man with hand to mouth. The creator speaks into a world still drowned in silence.

sentences.l: the-One · who-came-into-being · in(?) · the-sky · not · had-come-into-being · the-ground · the-mountains
sentences.i: the One who came into being in the sky when neither the ground nor the mountains had come into being;
sentences.n: wꜥ 'the One' is the harpoon wꜥ with its stroke and U15 standing for the complement ꜥ. ḫpr 'who came into being' is the participle (scarab and r). The next word is the crossed planks im, t and w: imytw 'between, in the midst of'. Budge reads àmtu and gives 'in', and that sense is taken here, with doubt, for 'in the sky' (pt: p, t and the sky sign). n ḫpr 'had not come into being': n (the arms held apart, with water n) before a sḏm·f denies a past event. sꜣṯw 'the ground' is the pintail duck sꜣ with t (for ṯ, as later scribes often write it), a small circle (approximate) and a stroke (Budge: set, 'the earth'). ḏww 'the mountains' is the mountain sign ḏw with a low hatched sign (approximated as O31; not read) and two strokes for the plural. The two subjects stand side by side with no 'and'. The god existed before the land rose out of the waters.

morph.gloss: mountain (noun m.; plural ḏww; the mountain sign)

sentences.l: the-Runner(?) · lord · sole · who-made · what-exists
sentences.i: the Runner(?), the sole lord, who made what exists,
sentences.n: The first word is a man walking with a stick over his shoulder (coded A33, an approximation), the curl w and U15. Budge reads peḥreru with his own query and gives 'runner'; no sign in the print gives the sounds pḥrr, and the walking man is taken as a word-sign for pḥrrw 'runner', 'he who runs (his course)', following Budge with the same doubt. nb wꜥ 'the sole lord': nb 'lord' and wꜥ 'one, sole' (harpoon, stroke and U15 for ꜥ) after it. ir 'who made' is the eye alone, the participle of iri. wnnt 'what exists' is the hare wn with two water-lines n, t and plural strokes: the feminine participle of wnn 'be' used as a noun, 'that which is'. Budge's numeral 12 stands before the first word.

sentences.l: has-fashioned · he · the-tongue · of-the-Ennead · of-the-gods
sentences.i: he has fashioned the tongue of the Ennead of the gods,
sentences.n: nb·n·f 'he has fashioned' is the sḏm·n·f of nbi 'fashion, mould, cast': the broad collar of gold on its stand (the sign nb, S12, approximate), foot b as complement and U15 as classifier, then n and ·f; Budge prints it as one word, nub-nef. The gold sign writes the verb because metal is cast in a mould. ns 'the tongue' is a horizontal sign with a hooked end (the tongue, F20, approximate; it is drawn like the hoe mr) with a stroke and a small curl (approximate). psḏt 'the Ennead' is a circle divided by a line, coded X6 by the house ruling for Budge's paut and close in shape to the sign psḏ (N9), with t: the company of nine gods. Budge reads paut and gives 'cycle'. nṯrw 'of the gods' follows directly as a genitive. The tongue is the organ of speech, by which the gods create.

sentences.l: who-draws-out · what-is · in · the-water
sentences.i: who draws out what is in the water.
sentences.n: ḫnp is the placenta ḫ, water n and p, with a nose sign (D19, approximate) and the papyrus roll as classifiers: a participle, 'who takes, who draws out' (Budge: χenp, 'drawing out'). The sense of ḫnp here is not certain. nty 'what, that which' (water n, t, two strokes y) is the relative adjective used as a noun; m mw 'in the water': mw is the three water-lines. The creator brings the world up out of the primeval waters.

sentences.l: come-forth · you · from · it · upon · the-flood-land(?) · of · the-lake · of-Horus
sentences.i: You come forth from it upon the flood-land(?) of the Lake of Horus.
sentences.n: pr·k 'you come forth' is the house pr with r as complement and ·k: the sḏm·f of pri. im·f 'from it' is the preposition m in its form before a suffix, written with the reed i and the owl, and ·f, referring to the water. ḥr 'upon' (face and stroke). npt is water n, a long rounded oblong (approximated as N18), p, t, a small hourglass-like sign (approximated as N23) and a stroke: Budge reads nept and gives 'the inundated land'. The word is not known otherwise and its sense is taken from Budge. nt is the feminine genitive, agreeing with npt. š 'lake' is the pool sign with t and a stroke; the t is not read (Budge: śet). ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon with the seated god. The Lake of Horus is a water of the sky from which the sun comes up.

sentences.l: breathe · I · the-breath · coming-forth · from · nose · your · the-north-wind · coming-forth · from · mother · your
sentences.i: I breathe the breath that comes forth from your nose, the north wind that comes forth from your mother.
sentences.n: tpi·i 'I breathe in' is t, p and the reed i with the nose (D19, approximate) as classifier, then the seated man ·i: the sḏm·f of a verb tpi 'breathe, inhale' (Budge: tepà, 'I smell'). nfw 'the breath, the air' is the sail (P5, approximate), the sign of wind and breath, with w and a stroke. pr 'which comes forth' is the participle of pri (house, r, legs), agreeing with nfw; prt, with t, agrees with the feminine mḥyt. m fnḏ·k 'from your nose': fnḏ is the nose sign with its stroke. mḥyt 'the north wind' is the sign mḥ (V22, approximate), the wick ḥ as complement, two reeds y, t and the sail. m mwt·k 'from your mother' (vulture mwt, t, ·k). The cool north wind of Egypt is the breath of life; it comes from the sun and from the sky.

sentences.l: may-glorify · you · spirit · my · may-make-divine · you · the-Osiris · ba · my
sentences.i: May you glorify my spirit; may you make divine the Osiris, my ba.
sentences.n: sꜣḫ·k 'may you glorify' is the bolt s, the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ as complement, the papyrus roll and ·k: the sḏm·f of sꜣḫ 'make (someone) an ꜣḫ, glorify', the causative of ꜣḫ, used for a wish. ꜣḫ·i 'my spirit' is the ibis with its stroke, a squatting man holding a flail (approximated) and ·i: the ꜣḫ, the dead as a shining and effective spirit. nṯri·k is the flag nṯr with t (for ṯ) and r as complements, two strokes y, the roll and ·k: nṯri 'be divine', here with an object, 'make divine'; the sense follows the parallel sꜣḫ·k ꜣḫ·i, but nṯri is a verb of quality and the use is not certain (Budge: 'make strong'). Wsir is the low seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye with a stroke. It is taken as the dead man himself, 'the Osiris', with bꜣ·i 'my ba' (the jabiru bꜣ, with the small pot before it in the type, and ·i) in apposition; Budge takes Wsir as an address to the god, 'thou Osiris'. ꜣḫ and ba are two of the forms in which the dead live on.

sentences.l: adoring · you · at-rest · lord · of-the-gods · exalting · you · for · wonders · your
sentences.i: Praise to you, at rest, O lord of the gods, and exaltation to you for your wonders!
sentences.n: dwꜣ tw 'praise to you' as in line 2, split from one group of Budge's; the star is printed as a six-rayed asterisk. ḥtp 'at rest' (offering table, t, p) is taken as the stative, 'being at rest, having set', with its ending unwritten; Budge supplies '[in]' before it. nb nṯrw 'lord of the gods', an address. sqꜣ tw 'exalting you': sqꜣ 'make high, exalt', the causative of qꜣi 'be high', is the bolt s and the hill-slope q with a man raising both arms and a flat bar with a small tuft (approximated as Aa13; not read) as classifiers, the ꜣ unwritten; tw (t and the curl w) is the pronoun object. Budge prints the two as one word, seqa-tu, and takes it as passive ('thou art exalted'); they are split here, built like dwꜣ tw. m biꜣwt·k 'for your wonders': biꜣwt is a sledge carrying a box with an animal head on top (the sign biꜣ, U16, approximate), t and plural strokes, the plural of biꜣyt 'wonder, marvel', and ·k. The hymn turns to the sun at evening.

sentences.l: may-shine · you · rays · upon · breast · my · like · the-day
sentences.i: May you shine with rays upon my breast, as by day.
sentences.n: Two words of the same root stand side by side. The first is the pierced hide st (F29), t, w, the sun with hanging rays (approximate), a stroke and ·k: taken as a verb, the sḏm·f of wish, 'may you shine, send out rays', from sti 'shoot, cast'; it is spelled like the noun. The second, stwt 'rays' (hide st, w, the rays and a stroke), is the noun, used as the means: 'shine (with) rays'. Budge too reads a verb and a noun ('shine thou [with thy] beams'). ḥr šnbt·i 'upon my breast' (šnbt as in line 2, now with ·i). mi hrw 'like the day': mi 'like' is the milk-jug in its net; hrw 'day' is the sun with a stroke. Budge gives 'daily' for the two words together; 'as by day' takes them as written. Ani asks to be lit by the sun even as it goes down.

morph.gloss: to cast rays, shine (verb; spelled like stwt 'rays')

sentences.l: the-Osiris · scribe · reckoning · the-god's-offerings · of · the-gods · all · overseer · of-the-Double-Granary · of · the-lords · of-Abydos
sentences.i: — the Osiris, the scribe who reckons the god's offerings of all the gods, overseer of the Double Granary of the lords of Abydos,
sentences.n: Ani is named with his titles, in apposition to the 'my' of the line before: these are the words of the man himself. Wsir (low seat Q2, approximate, over the eye) and sš 'scribe' (the palette). ḥsb 'reckon, count' is an oval with a small ring (approximated as Aa2) over a flat bar with a tuft (approximated as Aa13), taken as the word-sign of ḥsb with a classifier; sš ḥsb is the 'scribe who reckons', the accountant. ḥtp-nṯr 'the god's offerings' joins two of Budge's words: the offering table ḥtp with t and p, then the flag nṯr with the seated god; here the flag is written after ḥtp, in the order of reading. n nṯrw nbw 'of all the gods'. imy-r 'overseer' is the hoe mr alone (U6), which writes the title imy-r, 'he who is in the mouth', the man whose word is obeyed; Budge reads mer. šnwty 'the Double Granary' is two domed silos on a platform (the sign šnwt, O51, approximate) with t and two strokes for the dual (Budge: śenti, 'the granary'): the store of temple grain. n nbw ꜣbḏw 'of the lords of Abydos': ꜣbḏw is the Abydos emblem, a wig on a pole with plumes (R17, approximate), with the town sign; the lords of Abydos are its gods.

sentences.l: the-king's · scribe · true · beloved-of-him · Ani · true-of-voice · in · peace
sentences.i: true royal scribe, beloved of him, Ani, true of voice, in peace.
sentences.n: sš nswt 'royal scribe' is written with the sedge nswt 'king' first, out of respect, though it is read second; the sedge stands alone. mꜣꜥ 'true, real' is the plinth alone (no sickle printed), after the title it qualifies. mry·f 'his beloved, whom he loves' is the canal sign mr (N36) with a stroke and ·f: the passive participle of mri 'love', its y unwritten; 'he' is the king. ꜣny 'Ani' here has a squatting man holding a flail as classifier. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice, vindicated' is the plinth above the oar, no sickle printed: said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement. m ḥtp 'in peace' (Aa15 m and the offering table) ends the hymn to Ra.

sentences.l: adoring · Osiris · lord · of-everlastingness
sentences.i: Adoring Osiris, lord of everlastingness:
sentences.n: A second hymn begins, to Osiris; its first word is written in red, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. dwꜣ 'adore' is spelled out here: the hand d and a lasso-like loop taken as the sign wꜣ (V4, approximate), then the star as classifier, the chick w (not read; Budge: ṭuau), a man raising both arms (approximated) and the papyrus roll; it is the infinitive, as in the title of the hymn to Ra. Wsir 'Osiris' is the eye ir over the seat ws, with the seated god. nb ḏt 'lord of everlastingness': ḏt is the cobra ḏ, t and the land sign, time that stays for ever unchanged.

sentences.l: Wennefer · Horakhty · many · of-forms · great · of-shapes
sentences.i: Wennefer, Horakhty, many of forms and great of shapes,
sentences.n: wnn-nfr 'Wennefer' (Budge: Un-nefer), 'he who is (always) perfect', is the hare wn over two water-lines, the heart-and-windpipe nfr and the seated god, as in the hymn to Osiris on Plate 2. ḥr-ꜣḫty 'Horakhty' is spelled out here: the falcon ḥr, the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, t, two strokes y and two flat dotted ovals (coded N18, approximate) as classifiers; Budge prints Ḥeru - χuti with a hyphen, and it is kept as one word. Osiris is given the sun's name: the two gods meet in the night. ꜥšꜣ ḫprw 'many of forms' and ꜥꜣ irw 'great of shapes' are adjective-and-noun phrases. ꜥšꜣ 'many' is the lizard with plural strokes; ḫprw 'forms' as in the hymn to Ra. ꜥꜣ 'great' is a lozenge-tipped rod (the column ꜥꜣ, O29, approximate) with U15 standing for the complement ꜥ and a flat bar with a tie; irw 'shapes, forms' is the reed i as complement, the eye ir, w, a standing wrapped figure, the roll and a stroke.

sentences.l: Ptah · Sokar · Atum · in · Iunu
sentences.i: Ptah-Sokar-Atum in Iunu,
sentences.n: Three gods named as one. ptḥ 'Ptah' is p, t and the wick ḥ. skr 'Sokar' (Budge: Sekri) is the bolt s, the basket k, r and two strokes, with the boat of Sokar on its sledge as classifier (approximated as P3); the two strokes are not read. itm 'Atum' is t, the sledge tm and the seated god. iwnw 'Iunu', Heliopolis, is the pillar iwn, the pot nw and the town sign. Ptah of Memphis, Sokar of its cemetery and Atum of Heliopolis are joined in Osiris.

sentences.l: lord · of-the-Shetayt · joins(?) · he · Memphis
sentences.i: lord of the Shetayt; he is joined(?) with Memphis.
sentences.n: šṯyt 'the Shetayt' (Budge: śeθit, 'the hidden house') is the pool sign š (a long rectangle with oblique hatching, approximate), the rope ṯ, two reeds y, t and a house-like sign: the shrine of Sokar in the cemetery of Memphis, whose name was taken to mean 'the hidden place'. ḫnm·f is the jug ḫnm with m as complement, the roll and ·f, a sḏm·f: ḫnm 'join, unite with', 'he joins Memphis', the god coming to his city. Budge gives 'he hath created', as if from the potter-god's verb; the sense of the line is not certain. ḥwt-kꜣ-ptḥ 'Memphis', 'the Mansion of the ka of Ptah', is written inside the enclosure ḥwt: p and t, the wick ḥ, then the raised arms kꜣ over the town sign, Ptah printed before ka.

sentences.l: the-gods · are(?) · the-guides · of-the-Duat
sentences.i: The gods are(?) the guides of the Duat;
sentences.n: nṯrw 'the gods' is the flag three times, with the seated god and a stroke. pw (p and the chick w) is the word that links the two halves of a sentence without a verb, 'A pw B', 'A is B'; Budge gives it no English, and how it is meant here is not clear. sšm 'lead, guide' is the bolt s as complement, a blade on a support with a hooked end (the sign sšm, T32, approximate and doubtful), m as complement and the walking legs: taken as the participle 'guiding, guide', its plural ending unwritten (Budge: sem, 'guide of'). dwꜣt 'the Duat' (star, t and a house-like sign) is the world through which the sun and the dead pass by night. Budge reads 'he hath created Memphis and the gods, guide of the underworld'; read as written, it is the gods who lead the way below.

morph.gloss: to lead, guide (verb); guide, leader (participle used as a noun)

sentences.l: protect · they · you · set · you · in · Nut
sentences.i: they protect you when you set in Nut.
sentences.n: Budge prints χu-sen-tu as one group; it is split here into the verb with its suffix and tw 'you'. The verb is the placenta ḫ over a bent arm (coded D41, approximate), the chick w and a knotted upright (coded T3, approximate), then ·sn 'they' (bolt s, water n, plural strokes): ḫw 'protect, guard', the sḏm·f of ḫwi, with the arm and the upright as classifiers of force. Budge gives 'they glorify'; both his reading and the signs are doubtful. ·sn refers to the gods of the line before. tw (t and w) is the pronoun object. ḥtp·k 'you set' is a sḏm·f standing as a clause of time, 'when you set'. m nwt 'in Nut': nwt is written with water n and the town sign, as in the hymn to Ra. At sunset the sun enters the body of the sky-goddess.

sentences.l: embraces · you · Isis · in · peace
sentences.i: Isis embraces you in peace,
sentences.n: Budge prints ḥepti-θ as one group; it is split here into the verb and ṯw 'you'. ḥpt 'embrace' is the wick ḥ, p, t, two strokes (not read) and the embracing arms (approximated). ṯw is the rope ṯ alone, the older form of the pronoun tw, with its w unwritten; as in ḥpt tw mꜣꜥt, the object comes before the noun subject. ꜣst 'Isis' is the seat with t, an egg and a seated goddess (approximated). m ḥtp 'in peace'. Isis, the wife of Osiris, holds him as the sun goes down.

sentences.l: drives-away · she · the-opponents · from · the-mouth · of-paths · your
sentences.i: and she drives away the adversaries from the mouth of your paths.
sentences.n: sḥr·s 'she drives away' is the bolt s, the face ḥr with r as complement, the chick w (not read) and a man striking with a stick (approximated), then the bolt ·s 'she', Isis: the sḏm·f of sḥr 'drive away, remove'. ḏꜣyw 'the opponents' is the fire-drill ḏꜣ (U28, approximate) with ꜣ as complement, two reeds y and a kneeling enemy (approximated), the plural of ḏꜣy 'one who opposes', from ḏꜣi 'cross, oppose' (Budge: t'ai, 'the fiends'). m rꜣ wꜣwt·k 'from the mouth of your paths': rꜣ 'mouth, opening' is the mouth with its stroke; wꜣwt is the road wꜣt with t and plural strokes, and ·k. Budge's numeral 4 stands before m. The entrance to the god's roads is kept clear for him.

sentences.l: have-set · you · face · your · towards · the-West
sentences.i: You have set your face towards the West,
sentences.n: di·n·k 'you have set' is the arm holding a conical loaf (di, the sign of rdi 'give, put'), water n and ·k: the sḏm·n·f. Budge prints it as one word, ṭā-nek, 'thou givest'. rdi ḥr 'put the face' is 'turn towards'. ḥr·k 'your face' (face, stroke, ·k); r 'towards'. imntt 'the West' is the standard of the West with a falcon on it (R13, approximate), two t's and the hill-country sign. The West is the land of the dead, where the sun goes at evening.

sentences.l: brighten · you · the-Two-Lands · with · fine-gold
sentences.i: and you make the Two Lands bright with fine gold.
sentences.n: sḥḏ·k 'you brighten' is the bolt s, a knotted upright taken as the mace ḥḏ (T3, approximate) with the cobra ḏ as complement, the sun with hanging rays and ·k: the causative of ḥḏ 'be bright', a sḏm·f. Budge reads seḥet'-k. tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt, is the land sign written twice, with no ending written. The last word's first sign is coded M21 (approximate and doubtful), a tall thin stem with a hooked tip and a small loop at its foot; then the bead-collar of gold, a small circle and plural strokes. Budge reads smu and gives 'smu metal'. The stem with a hooked head is taken here as the sceptre that writes ḏꜥm, as in the hymn to Osiris on Plate 2, where ḏꜥm 'fine gold' has the same collar and grains; read ḏꜥm, with that doubt. The setting sun lights the land below with the colour of gold.

sentences.l: those-who-lie-down · stand-up · to · see · to-you
sentences.i: Those who lie (in death) stand up to look upon you;
sentences.n: sḏryw 'those who lie down' is the bolt s, a bundle-like sign taken as ḏr (M36, approximate) with r as complement, two reeds y and a lying animal, perhaps the lion (approximated as E22), with a stroke: the plural participle of sḏr 'lie down, spend the night', a name for the dead (Budge: st'eriu, 'the dead'). ꜥḥꜥ 'stand up' is the mast-like sign ꜥḥꜥ, U15 where the arm ꜥ is read as complement, and the walking legs: a sḏm·f after its subject. r mꜣꜣ 'to see': the eye with the sickle mꜣ over it, and two vultures ꜣ. Then water n and ·k: Budge prints maa-nek as one group, and it is split here into mꜣꜣ and n·k 'to you'. Where an object pronoun is expected (mꜣꜣ·k 'seeing you'), the papyrus has n·k; the same comes in line 5. Either the n is a later way of joining the object, or the verb is mꜣn, a later spelling of 'see'; either way the sense is 'to look upon you'. At the sunset the dead below rise to greet the god.

sentences.l: breathe · they · the-north-wind(?) · see · they · face · your · like · the-rising · of-the-Disk · in · horizon · his
sentences.i: they breathe the north wind(?), and they see your face like the rising of the Disk in his horizon.
sentences.n: tpi·sn 'they breathe' is t, p, the reed i and the nose sign, with ·sn 'they'; Budge's numeral 5 is printed between the nose and the suffix. mḥw is the sign mḥ (V22, approximate), w and a stroke; it is taken as a short writing of mḥyt 'the north wind', the breath of life, as in the hymn to Ra (Budge: meḥu, 'the airs'), and the reading is not certain. mꜣꜣ·sn ḥr·k 'they see your face': eye and sickle, ·sn, and ḥr·k. mi wbn itn 'like the rising of the Disk': mi 'like' is the milk-jug with a reed as complement; wbn is the infinitive, and itn 'the Disk' (reed i, t, n and the sun-disk) its subject as a direct genitive. m ꜣḫt·f 'in his horizon': ꜣḫt with ·f. To the dead below, the coming of the sun is a sunrise.

sentences.l: hearts · their · at-peace · upon · seeing · to-you
sentences.i: Their hearts are at peace at the sight of you.
sentences.n: ib·sn 'their hearts' (the heart with its stroke and ·sn) is the subject of ḥtp 'are at peace', a stative after its subject (offering table, t, p). ḥr mꜣꜣ n·k 'upon seeing you': ḥr 'on account of, at' with the infinitive mꜣꜣ, written here with the eye alone as a word-sign (no sickle printed), and n·k as in line 4, split from Budge's single group maa-nek.

sentences.l: you · eternity · everlastingness
sentences.i: You are eternity and everlastingness.
sentences.n: ntk 'you' is the independent pronoun (water n, t, the basket k): ntk N, 'you are N', is a sentence with no verb. nḥḥ 'eternity' is the wick ḥ twice with the sun-disk between them as classifier of time, the water n of the word unwritten, as on Plate 2; ḏt 'everlastingness' is the cobra ḏ, t and the land sign. The two words stand side by side with no 'and': nḥḥ is time that comes round again and again, like the sun, ḏt time that stays, like Osiris; the god is both.
